title: The Hidden 'GitLost' Attack Leaking Private GitHub Code via AI!
summary: Cybersecurity researchers at Noma Security discovered 'GitLost,' an indirect prompt injection vulnerability affecting GitHub's Agentic Workflows. The flaw allows hidden commands in public issues to trick privileged AI agents into posting private source code publicly.
raw_text: So check this out, developers! Security researchers just uncovered a major flaw called 'GitLost' that targets GitHub's new AI Agentic Workflows. Here’s how it works: attackers embed sneaky, obfuscated commands inside public GitHub issues. When GitHub’s autonomous AI agent reads the issue to summarize it for a developer, it gets tricked into thinking those malicious instructions are system commands. The agent then accesses the company's private code repositories and leaks secret API keys and proprietary algorithms right into public comment threads! Here’s the wild part: traditional firewalls can’t stop this because current transformer models mathematically struggle to separate trusted system prompts from untrusted user input within the same context window. It's a huge reminder that as we give AI agents autonomous access to our developer tools, input sanitization is going to be the ultimate battleground for dev security. Are you using AI agents in your dev workflow yet?
